## Question and scope

Can the saved baseline-versus-selected-head comparison be reproduced from
pinned public inputs and unchanged historical model code? This report replays
the development evaluation of two fixed programs. It does not rerun the LLM
search, train the GluFormer encoder, or evaluate a new independent test cohort.

```{python}
import json
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
root = Path.cwd()
if not (root / "config/project.json").exists():
    root = root.parent
replay = json.loads((root / "results/replay.json").read_text())
audit = json.loads((root / "results/data_audit.json").read_text())
display(Markdown(f"Pinned source commit: `{replay['source_commit']}`. "
                 f"Evaluation: **{replay['n_seeds']} seeds × {replay['n_folds']} folds**. "
                 f"Matched normalized IDs: **{audit['matched_normalized_ids']}**; "
                 f"embedding dimensions: **{audit['embedding_dimensions']}**."))
matched = all(value["record_matched_within_tolerance"] for value in replay["models"].values())
display(Markdown("**Exact historical-number check: " + ("PASS" if matched else "FAIL") + ".** "
                 "A successful report build does not change this result. "
                 "The cause of any metric discrepancy remains unresolved."))
```

## Computed replay

```{python}
rows = []
for model, info in replay["models"].items():
    for metric, value in info["metrics"].items():
        rows.append({"model": model, "metric": metric,
                     "recorded": info["recorded_metrics"][metric],
                     "replayed": value,
                     "difference": info["difference_from_record"][metric]})
table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
display(table.style.format({"recorded": "{:.6f}", "replayed": "{:.6f}", "difference": "{:+.6f}"}).hide(axis="index"))
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Historical development-CV correlations for the fixed baseline and selected candidate. The inputs differ and the historical target-scaling problem is preserved."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bars compare replayed Pearson and Spearman correlations for the historical baseline and selected candidate. They are development metrics, not independent test results."
plot = table[table.metric.isin(["pearson_r", "spearman_r"])].pivot(index="metric", columns="model", values="replayed")
ax = plot.plot.bar(rot=0, ylim=(0, 1), figsize=(7, 4))
ax.set_ylabel("Historical development-CV correlation")
ax.set_xlabel("")
ax.legend(title="Fixed program")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Interpretation limits

The selected candidate adds a GMI predictor that the original baseline does not
use. The original search repeatedly reused these folds, and the historical
harness standardizes training targets per fold without restoring predictions
to the original units before pooling. The replay preserves these choices to
test reproducibility, not to endorse the scores. The quantity named
`prediction_stability` is one minus the standard deviation of Pearson
correlations across seeds; it is not clinical stability.

The primary archive names each recording with a participant identifier, period
and date. The historical normalization drops the first character and retains
part of the period/date. The filename audit confirms both merging of distinct
participants and splitting of repeated records from the same participant.
The old replay above preserves this defective grouping. It must not be used
as a reliable estimate of predictive quality. The GMI CSV stores IDs in rounded
scientific notation, so its exact dates cannot all be recovered; its participant
and period prefixes match the primary archive.

```{python}
input_table = pd.DataFrame(audit["inputs"]).T.rename_axis("file").reset_index()
input_table["file"] = input_table["file"].map({
    "GluFormer_Representations_Shanghai_2023.csv": "Embeddings",
    "Shanghai_GMI.csv": "GMI",
    "Shanghai_results.csv": "HbA1c",
})
columns = ["file", "rows", "normalized_unique_ids", "participant_ids_from_archive_prefix",
           "historical_groups_merging_distinct_participants", "participants_split_across_historical_groups"]
compact = input_table[columns].copy()
compact.columns = ["Input", "Rows", "Old groups", "Participants", "Mixed groups", "Split persons"]
display(compact.style.hide(axis="index"))
```

The next stage is a separately labelled evaluation with corrected target units
and matched input baselines. Reusing these development data cannot establish
an independent confirmation of the original model search.
